status: Six native view-dispatch workflows and real-browser integration verified. Full shortcut, scheduling and application parity remain unfinished.

reference.press: 0x44b350, raw LLVM assembly; Ghidra does not define this procedure.
reference.release: 0x44b470, raw LLVM assembly; an initial query at 0x44b480 was not the entry and was rejected.
reference.observed: Six fresh-process-repeat workflows establish actual Qt modifier normalization, temporary Pan, persistent restore tool, B/V event flags, Primary/Base/Current layer separation, mode-10 and batch guards. Direct key dispatch does not activate the A/D Qt shortcut path in the owned hidden window.

actions.25: Construct public QKeyEvent and synchronously dispatch to the actual owned VmMainView. Record resulting tool, histories and auxiliary input state.
actions.27: Read Primary/Base/Current layer IDs plus actual layer-button enabled and view-focus getters.
actions.28: Invoke an observed integer/bool/void VmMainView Qt slot.
actions.29: Invoke an observed integer/bool/void MainModel Qt slot.
actions.30: Dispatch a real constructed QFocusEvent. Direct focus-in/out events preserve captured keyboard state; OS window activation remains unverified.

capture.constraints: No OS keyboard injection, foreground activation or original installation changes. Preserve existing action wires and accepted helper snapshots. Expected state is only an assertion.

implementation: ViewerInput owns keyboard/layer state; React renders snapshots. Browser pointer and key producers share viewerModifiers. Tool changes enter the existing ordered document gesture queue. Current tool and Primary/Base/Current layers are separate.

rules.press: Update Shift state from current event modifiers. Set held B/V flags from this key only, clearing the other flag. Change current layer only for an enabled B/V target. With Shift and a non-Pan tool, retain the tool and enter Pan.
rules.release: Clear the matching B/V flag. Restore Base layer only when neither remains. When Shift is absent, restore the retained tool if the prior Shift flag is set and the current tool is Pan; then clear the Shift flag.
rules.restoreLifetime: Retained Pan restore tool is not reset when the user later selects Pan. A subsequent Shift press/release from Pan can therefore restore the earlier tool. Selecting another tool during temporary Pan prevents restoration on release.
rules.modifiers: B/V still process with Ctrl/Alt/Meta, and repeated key events are not skipped.
rules.guards: Mode 10 and the native batch flag suppress viewer key changes. Qt shortcuts, pointer pan movement, focus loss and processing-time routing remain separate verification work.

verification.remaining: Qt A/D/etc shortcut activation, normal OS focus/window deactivation, processing-time routing, layer-button pointer press/release semantics and broader editable-widget focus contexts.
verification.layerRouting: Static original input/sampling dataflow and an isolated before/after browser check establish the bounded layer-independent admission correction. Held B/V in that browser check use declared DOM key events, not trusted key holds or new native pointer capture. See ../evidence/layer-routing-browser-verification.json and viewer-layer-code-review.md.

pointerProducer.contract: Use one PointerEvent producer for first, intermediate and final button changes. A changed button with its held-state bit set is a press; a cleared bit is a release. A button value of -1 is movement. Convert DOM left/middle/right button indices to the existing Qt-style bit values 1/4/2 and preserve the full held-button mask and current modifiers. Tools use the left held bit, regardless of which button caused the press. Pan starts on a changed left press and ends on any release, matching the pinned Qt 4.4.3 ScrollHandDrag implementation. Keep the existing gesture wire and capture owner.
